title: HVAC Service Call Form
subtitle: Residential HVAC Service Call: captures actual activity and handoff.
description: HVAC Service Call Form covers heating or cooling unit, thermostat, duct path, condensate, and occupied comfort zone. The home-service coordinator records Residential HVAC Service Call activity, quantities, variance, and handoff. HVAC Service Call Form keeps Residential HVAC Service Call exceptions visible until the home-service coordinator handoff.
use_case: Use HVAC Service Call Form at residence, equipment location, thermostat zone, and exterior unit area. Document heating or cooling unit, thermostat, duct path, condensate, and occupied comfort zone identity before Residential HVAC Service Call begins. Compare heating or cooling unit, thermostat, duct path, condensate, and occupied comfort zone findings with stated Residential HVAC Service Call criteria; route unresolved Residential HVAC Service Call issues to qualified HVAC technician. For HVAC Service Call Form, confirm requirements for Residential HVAC Service Call. Ask qualified HVAC technician to review Residential HVAC Service Call conditions beyond the home-service coordinator's role.

blocks.label: Residential HVAC Service Call operating checks
items: Thermostat call, displayed temperature, and mode response
Filter, airflow, register, and return condition
Indoor and outdoor unit visual condition
Condensate, drain, water, and icing observation
Electrical, fuel, venting, noise, and odor concern
Supply-return temperature or authorized performance result
blocks.guidance: Complete the Residential HVAC Service Call checks that apply to this heating or cooling unit, thermostat, duct path, condensate, and occupied comfort zone activity; explain every unchecked required item.

blocks.label: Do not proceed without control
blocks.guidance: Stop normal processing when a fuel, electrical, refrigerant, water, access, or safe-operation concern remains. Protect heating or cooling unit, thermostat, duct path, condensate, and occupied comfort zone; document the Residential HVAC Service Call notification and await qualified HVAC technician direction.

blocks.label: Stop, hold, or correction triggers
items: Gas odor, combustion, damaged conductor, or water damage
System cannot be tested or restored safely
blocks.guidance: For Residential HVAC Service Call, identify affected heating or cooling unit, thermostat, duct path, condensate, and occupied comfort zone scope; ask home-service coordinator to document the Residential HVAC Service Call immediate control before continuing.
